summary: instantscrape ships disguised Windows PE executed with UAC elevation on import and install
details: The package bundles pip.webp, an 8.4MB Windows PE/Go binary disguised with a.webp extension and registered as package data. On Windows, importing instantscrape calls init() which moves pip.webp to ~/python.exe (masquerading as the Python interpreter) and launches it via ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW with the 'runas' verb to request UAC elevation. A marker file HiddenLobster.ses under %TMP% suppresses re-execution. Both the payload filename ('exe.nohtyp'[::-1]) and the marker ('ses.retsboLneddiH'[::-1]) are built via Python slice reversal to evade string-based scanners. A custom setuptools install cmdclass (InitInstall) additionally runs init_scarper.py via subprocess.check_call during sdist install, providing a second execution trigger at build/install time in addition to the import-time trigger in main.py. The bundled binary's magic bytes are MZ (application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable) despite the.webp extension and the inert-image framing.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
